project: Cut Functional-Lane Wall Time Without Weakening Evidence
description: Restore Go test caching on the default functional lane, add an explicit fresh functional target for authoritative execution, replace a measured set of high-impact fixed sleeps with bounded observable-condition waits, and publish reproducible timing evidence while preserving assertions, coverage, CI semantics, and lane ownership. The intent is to shorten every coding and review feedback cycle without weakening behavioral proof.

context.customerAsk: Split cached and fresh functional targets, preserve fresh semantics wherever CI or documentation requires them, replace high-impact fixed-sleep polling with bounded observation-driven waits, and record cold, warm, and per-package timing evidence without weakening tests or coverage.
context.problem: The default make test-functional path and cmd/functionallane both force -count=1, preventing Go from reusing successful results for unchanged packages. Observable asynchronous functional scenarios also use fixed sleeps that add avoidable worst-case latency. Agents and reviewers therefore repeatedly pay nearly the full functional-suite cost, while the CI functional coverage path is roughly 4.5 minutes.
context.solution: Make the default runner omit go test -count so normal cache validity applies; add make test-functional-fresh with explicit -count=1; keep authoritative CI and coverage workflows fresh; use timing artifacts to select a small number of slow packages and replace only directly observable waits with bounded diagnostic observers; then record comparable cold, warm, fresh, and package timing results. Preserve the full suite, assertions, coverage floor, failure behavior, and JavaScript durability lane ownership.

acceptanceCriteria: A normal make test-functional run omits go test -count, and a second run with no relevant input change reports cached package results and completes at least 70% faster than the recorded cold run in the same environment.
make test-functional-fresh explicitly runs the same boundary check and maintained short functional package set with -count=1, and repeated fresh runs execute rather than reuse cached results.
Required CI, functional coverage, and documented workflows that require unconditional execution retain fresh semantics, package scope, short mode, timeouts, failure propagation, and coverage floors.

Fixed waits changed by this lane are limited to measured high-impact packages and directly observable conditions; they return promptly on success, fail within a generous bound with useful diagnostics, and retain every scenario assertion.

Comparable evidence records cold and warm default wall time, a fresh run, and before/after functional-timing-summary.json results; every touched performance-target package shows reduced representative wall time.
The lane does not modify tests/functional/orchestration/javascript/durability, lower coverage, weaken assertions, mechanically churn all sleep sites, or include unrelated cleanup.

Quality gate: Typecheck passes; Tests pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green; the full functional suite and required CI checks pass.

Delivery: the implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file contention are resolved against current origin/main, generated files are regenerated rather than hand-merged if encountered, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Separate cached and fresh functional execution
userStories.description: As a coding agent, I want the default functional command to reuse valid Go test results while retaining an explicit fresh command so repeated evidence gathering is fast without removing the ability to force execution.
acceptanceCriteria: make test-functional runs the functional boundary check and maintained short functional suite without supplying a go test -count override.
make test-functional-fresh runs the same boundary check, package scope, job limit, short mode, and timeout while explicitly supplying -count=1.
cmd/functionallane omits -count when the caller does not request it, forwards a valid explicit count unchanged, and rejects invalid count input clearly.
Two back-to-back default runs with unchanged relevant inputs show cached package results on the warm run, while two fresh runs execute the packages both times.
Runner and target regression tests prove generated go test arguments and success/failure propagation for cached and fresh modes.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented cache-aware `cmd/functionallane` execution with count 0 as the default omission mode, positive explicit counts forwarded unchanged, and negative counts rejected before process launch. Added `make test-functional-fresh` with the same boundary check, package scope, jobs, short mode, timeout, and failure propagation as `make test-functional`, but with explicit `-count=1`. Added runner and Make-target regression coverage for cached/fresh command arguments and both success/failure paths. Focused runner tests, repository Go tests, vet, backend size/maintainability/file-count/structure gates, and Make dry-run verification pass. Full cold/warm/fresh timing evidence remains a project-level story 004 concern; the workstation's attempted full measurement hit untouched process-API-server timeouts under concurrent unrelated Go lanes, and typecheck is blocked by missing Bun type definitions.

userStories.title: Preserve fresh semantics for authoritative workflows
userStories.description: As a CI owner, I want workflows that produce authoritative functional evidence to keep forcing real execution so enabling the local cache does not weaken required checks.
acceptanceCriteria: Every required CI or repository workflow that invokes the ordinary functional lane and requires unconditional execution uses test-functional-fresh or an equivalent explicit -count=1 path.

Functional coverage and visualization execute the maintained short functional suite, generate coverage and timing artifacts from a real run, enforce the existing coverage floor, and fail on the same boundary, suite, coverage, metadata, or rendering failures as before.
Developer documentation distinguishes the fast cached feedback command from the fresh command and identifies fresh use for CI-equivalent evidence and flake investigation.
A representative failing functional test makes both cached and fresh targets exit non-zero; caching never converts a failure into success.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Preserved authoritative fresh semantics by making `cmd/gocoveragecheck` append `-count=1` to every instrumented coverage invocation; the existing CI `functional-test-viz` route therefore keeps its maintained short package discovery, timeout, coverage profile, timing JSON, package manifest, coverage floor, and fail-closed boundary/suite/render behavior. Updated Makefile comments and developer/functional documentation to distinguish cache-aware `make test-functional`, fresh `make test-functional-fresh`, and fresh coverage/visualization usage for CI-equivalent evidence and flake investigation. Added coverage timing-argument regression evidence and representative failing-test output checks for both cached and fresh targets. Focused coverage-check and runner tests, vet, Make dry-run, diff checks, and Linux cross-compilation of the POSIX contract tests pass; `make typecheck` remains blocked by the workstation's missing Bun type definitions (`TS2688`).

userStories.title: Replace high-impact fixed waits with bounded observations
userStories.description: As a contributor running functional tests, I want high-impact asynchronous scenarios to proceed when their observable condition is satisfied so tests do not pay a fixed delay after the system is ready.
acceptanceCriteria: A baseline timing summary ranks packages before edits, and implementation selects only a small set of the slowest packages with waits on observable event-stream, filesystem, HTTP readiness, process, or store state.

Selected waits use an existing specialized observer or a shared support wait that polls every 10-25 ms, accepts a generous explicit deadline, returns immediately after the condition is observed, and reports the last observation or error at timeout.
Tests for shared wait behavior prove immediate success, delayed success, timeout, and diagnostic failure behavior without relying on long real-time sleeps.
Each retained or introduced polling boundary includes an in-code justification for why deterministic observation or edge mocking cannot replace it.
Assertions and observable scenario outcomes in every touched functional test remain unchanged, and the lane does not touch tests/functional/orchestration/javascript/durability.
Focused functional tests for each touched package pass repeatedly without increasing flake incidence.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Captured the fresh functional timing summary at `.artifacts/functional-test-viz/story-003-before-functional-timing-summary.json` (142 packages, 207.342s wall time); the measured candidates selected for this story were `work/relationships` (43.950s), `work/submission` (33.606s), and `sessions/execution` (31.719s). Replaced their fixed 50–100ms public Work/Session polling sleeps with shared `support.WaitForObservation`, which observes immediately, polls every 10ms, preserves the bounded caller deadline, and reports the last observation and observer error on timeout. Added shared-wait coverage for immediate success, delayed success, timeout, and diagnostic observer failure. Repeated focused functional runs passed three times for all three touched packages; support tests, focused vet, backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, and pkg-structure passed. The repository typecheck remains blocked by the workstation's missing Bun type definitions (`TS2688`); the JavaScript durability package was not changed.

userStories.title: Prove throughput gains and preserved behavior
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want reproducible performance and correctness evidence so I can confirm the lane is materially faster and still trustworthy.
acceptanceCriteria: The PR records commands, environment-relevant context, and wall times for a cold default run, an unchanged warm default run, and a fresh run; the warm run is at least 70% faster than the cold run and visibly uses Go's test cache.
Before/after functional-timing-summary.json evidence is captured under comparable conditions and lists selected touched packages with reduced representative package wall times.
The full fresh functional suite passes after wait changes with the same package scope, short mode, assertions, timeout envelope, and coverage floor.
Required CI checks remain semantically equivalent and are terminal and green; variance or packages intentionally not optimized are documented rather than hidden by weakening evidence.
Scope review confirms no changes to the JavaScript durability owner package, no unrelated cleanup, and no hand-merged generated artifacts.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Focused post-change timing evidence is complete for the three packages changed by story 003: `.artifacts/functional-test-viz/story-004-after-focused-functional-timing-summary.json` reports complete fresh instrumented results for 3 packages (17.847s wall, 36.587s package elapsed sum), with `sessions/execution` 31.719s -> 13.386s, `work/relationships` 43.950s -> 13.004s, and `work/submission` 33.606s -> 10.197s. The same packages passed a three-repeat short focused run. Story remains incomplete because full `make test-functional` cold/warm attempts were contended or incomplete, and the full lane plus isolated three-repeat focused execution of `factory_runtime/root_composition` fails with the unchanged baseline provider-prompt mismatch (`unexpected provider prompt`: 18 calls); therefore no complete full fresh lane or full before/after timing summary can be claimed yet. Typecheck remains blocked by the workstation's missing Bun type definitions (`TS2688`).
